6763.t: Pre-Greek, likely Anatolian. Compare with Hittite 𒌷𒄭𒇷𒅅𒋡 (ᵁᴿᵁḫi-li-ik-ka₄ /⁠Ḫilika⁠/), and Luwian 𔗒𔔹𔗧𔔂 (hi-li-ka^(URBS) /⁠Ḫilikka⁠/) and 𔗒𔖱𔓯𔗧𔔂 (hi+ra/i-i-ka^(URBS) /⁠Ḫirikka⁠/).

6786.t: Likely of Anatolian origin, but of uncertain meaning: compare Hittite 𒇻𒊌𒅗𒊑 (“to light up”), and the placename Λυκαονία (Lukaonía) (related to Lukka).

6742.t: Likely derived from Proto-Celtic *galnati (“to be able”). See also Κελτός (Keltós) and Latin Gallus, which might be from the same source.

6703.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *sew-? Proto-Indo-European *sewH-? Proto-Indo-European *suH- Proto-Hellenic *hūs Ancient Greek ὗς (hûs) Proto-Indo-European *-nós Ancient Greek -νος (-nos) Proto-Indo-European *-is Proto-Indo-European *-h₂…

6715.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ser-? Proto-Indo-European *srew- Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ Proto-Indo-European *sréwmn̥? Proto-Hellenic *hréumə Ancient Greek ῥεῦμα From Proto-Hellenic *hréumə, likely inherited from Proto-Indo-European *sréwmn̥, from…

6734.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew גְּדֵרָה (gəḏērā). More at Γάδαρα (Gắdără).

6748.t: From δόσις (dósis, “gift”) + θεός (theós, “god”). For the semantics, compare Θεόδωρος (Theódōros).

6721.t: According to Beekes of Pre-Greek origin or related to Lithuanian ražis (“stubble”). Compare ῥαχός (rhakhós, “thorn hedge”).

6718.t: According to Beekes, if related to ῥοῖβδος (rhoîbdos, “buzzing, hissing noise”), this word is certainly of Pre-Greek origin, but even if unrelated, such an origin may still be considered.

6716.t: From Proto-Indo-European *wr̥h₁tós, from *werh₁- (“to speak, say”). Equivalent to εἴρω (eírō, “I say”) + -τός (-tós, verbal adjective suffix).

6711.t: Of ultimately onomatopoeic origin, perhaps via a Proto-Indo-European *sre(n)gʰ- (“to snore”), whence also perhaps Old Irish srennaid (“to snore”), Proto-West Germanic *snarkōn (“to snore, snort”), though Beekes also suggests a possible Pre-Greek origin.

6722.t: From ῥιζόω (rhizóō) + -μα (-ma). See Ancient Greek ῥίζα (rhĭ́ză).

6706.t: From ὑπο- (hupo-) + ὀπ- (op-, suppletive root of ὁράω (horáō)) + -τος (-tos).

6705.t: From ὑπο- (hŭpo-, “sub-, hypo-”) + αἶθρος (aîthros, “clear chill air”).
